title: unify-sdks-auth-retries-streaming-parity-v1.170.0
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: SDKs for Python/TypeScript/Go have drifted in behavior for auth propagation, retry semantics, and streaming ergonomics. Customers reported inconsistent retry behavior across languages and missing parity in streaming event types (ENG-3412, ENG-3420). This PR unifies the surface area and bumps all SDKs to v1.170.0.

What this PR does: - Centralizes auth header propagation and token refresh paths so all SDKs use the same hierarchical flow: explicit API key > environment token provider > credential helper. - Aligns retry policy defaults (idempotent method classification, exponential backoff parameters, and max attempts) across SDKs and exposes the same configuration knobs. - Brings streaming APIs into parity: consistent chunk/event envelope ("type","delta","error","done"), unified client-side cancel semantics, and improved backpressure handling in TS/Go. - Python ergonomics: adds context manager support for streaming clients, better async iterator compatibility, and clearer sync/async split. - TypeScript ergonomics: improves ReadableStream integration and typings for streaming callbacks. - Go ergonomics: stabilizes the StreamReceiver interface and improves cancellation propagation with contexts. - Adds comprehensive cross-language test vectors (recorded transcripts + replay harness) used in CI for parity checks.

Description (details): The changes touch SDK core modules and tests. Auth: replaced ad-hoc header additions with a shared AuthProvider abstraction in each SDK that follows the documented priority order. Retry: introduced RetryConfig with canonical defaults (initial_backoff=100ms, max_backoff=5s, multiplier=2.0, max_attempts=4) and standardized transient error classification (5xx, 429, network errors). Streaming: normalized event envelope and added helper utilities to map language-specific streaming primitives to the canonical envelope. Ergonomics: small API surface tweaks to make streaming usage consistent (Python: `with Client.streaming(...) as s:`, TS: async iterator support + `onEvent` convenience, Go: `StreamReceiver` interface and `Start/Stop` helpers).

Checklist:
- [x] Implement unified auth providers across Python/TS/Go
- [x] Implement and document retry defaults and config
- [x] Streaming envelope and helpers for all SDKs
- [x] Add cross-language parity tests and CI harness
- [x] Version bumps to v1.170.0 for all three SDK packages
- [x] Update CHANGELOGs and release notes

Testing:
- Unit tests added/updated in each SDK (python: tests/test_auth.py, tests/test_retries.py, tests/test_streaming_parity.py). TS and Go equivalents added. 
- Added cross-language integration parity suite (ci/parity/recordings/*.json) and a lightweight runner that verifies recorded transcripts for stable API outputs. 
- CI: initial run showed a flaky TS streaming test (backpressure timing). I adjusted the harness and re-ran; all checks passed on the final run.

Rollout and compatibility:
- This is backwards-compatible for existing call patterns. There are small ergonomics additions (context manager in Python, new event types) that are additive. Retry default changes tighten transient handling but keep configurable overrides. Documented in release notes.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on correctness of retry classification and streaming cancel semantics. The parity harness intentionally tolerates minor ordering differences if envelope semantics are preserved. See linked linear tickets for acceptance criteria.

review_comments: Ben Carlson: Please double-check the retry classification for 409 — I think some clients treat it as transient for optimistic concurrency. -> Response: We intentionally kept 409 as non-transient because it usually requires client action; added a note in docs and a config example for teams that want to treat 409 as transient.

Diego Marquez: TS streaming test still flaked on CI (backpressure). Can we add a small buffering window in the harness? -> Response: Added a 50ms soft-buffer in ci/parity/runner.py and re-recorded the fixtures; CI stabilized.

Riley Chen: Are there any GC/leak risks with the new Python context manager? -> Response: Added explicit close() in the teardown and extra tests to assert no dangling sockets; also added weakref-based finalizer as safety net.

Ops: no infra rollout required; server-side unchanged
